title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Hierarchical DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical additional dimension: temporal redundancy across frames. Existing video MLLM compression methods treat frames independently or use simple uniform sampling, ignoring both cross-frame redundancy and instruction-conditioned temporal relevance simultaneously. This leads to either missing key temporal events or retaining highly redundant consecutive frames.

Proposed Method: We propose TempCDPruner, a hierarchical two-stage DPP-based pruning framework for video MLLMs. Stage 1 (Frame-level): We construct a conditional similarity kernel across frames that combines visual feature similarity with instruction relevance scores, then apply DPP to select a diverse, instruction-relevant frame subset. Stage 2 (Token-level): Within each selected frame, we apply CDPruner-style spatial token pruning conditioned on the instruction. Crucially, we introduce a cross-frame diversity bonus in the token-level kernel to suppress tokens whose content already appeared in other retained frames, creating globally non-redundant token sets. Both stages remain training-free.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video. We measure accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs at various reduction ratios, compare against FastV, LLaVA-PruMerge, and temporal sampling baselines, and conduct ablations on the two-stage interaction and cross-frame diversity bonus.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical additional dimension—temporal redundancy across frames. Existing video MLLMs either uniformly sample frames or apply per-frame token pruning independently, ignoring cross-frame redundancy and temporal instruction relevance jointly. This leads to massive token counts (frames × spatial tokens) that bottleneck video MLLM inference.

Proposed Method: We extend CDPruner's conditional diversity framework to spatio-temporal token pruning via a hierarchical 3D DPP formulation. We define a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures (1) spatial similarity within frames, (2) temporal similarity across frames, and (3) instruction conditioning that weights tokens relevant to temporal queries (e.g., 'what happens after...'). We decompose the 3D DPP into a two-stage process: first selecting a diverse subset of keyframes via temporal DPP conditioned on the instruction, then applying spatial CDPruner within selected frames. An optional motion-aware kernel leverages optical flow features to further distinguish temporally salient tokens.

Experiments: Evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-Video backbones. Ablate temporal vs. spatial pruning stages, kernel designs, and reduction ratios. Compare against FastV, StreamingLLM-video, and per-frame CDPruner baselines on accuracy-FLOPs tradeoff curves.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video-Language Models via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video-language models face a compounded token explosion—a 60-second video at 1fps with 256 tokens/frame yields 15,360 visual tokens. Naive application of spatial pruning ignores temporal redundancy patterns unique to video (e.g., static backgrounds persisting across frames, motion-relevant regions tied to temporal queries like 'what happens after X'). Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to video by defining a joint spatio-temporal conditional similarity that captures both within-frame spatial redundancy and cross-frame temporal redundancy, conditioned on the language instruction. We formulate a hierarchical DPP: first applying temporal DPP to select diverse keyframes weighted by instruction relevance across time, then applying spatial conditional DPP within each selected frame. To handle motion-sensitive queries, we incorporate optical flow magnitude as a prior into the DPP kernel, upweighting tokens in high-motion regions. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and NExT-QA benchmarks using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-NeXT-Video backbones. We measure accuracy-vs-token-reduction tradeoffs, TTFT latency, and ablate temporal vs. spatial pruning contributions, targeting 90%+ token reduction while retaining 92%+ original accuracy.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively reduces visual token redundancy in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded challenge: massive temporal redundancy across frames multiplied by spatial redundancy within frames. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies, while joint pruning across all frames is computationally prohibitive due to the quadratic complexity of DPP. Proposed Method: We propose TemporalCDP, a hierarchical DPP-based token pruning framework for video MLLMs. First, we define spatio-temporal conditional similarity by conditioning visual token similarities on both the textual instruction and temporal position embeddings, capturing temporal dynamics alongside instruction relevance. Second, we decompose the joint DPP across all frames into a two-stage process: (1) frame-level selection using a coarse DPP that maximizes temporal diversity conditioned on the query, selecting a subset of keyframes; (2) token-level selection within chosen frames using CDPruner's spatial DPP. We further introduce a cross-frame token merging step that merges near-duplicate tokens identified across selected frames to avoid redundant temporal information. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and VideoLLaMA2 as backbones, measuring accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs at various reduction ratios, comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and uniform sampling baselines.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frame Sequences
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively addresses spatial visual token redundancy in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded challenge: massive token counts from temporal frame sequences (often 10-100x more tokens than images) where both spatial redundancy within frames AND temporal redundancy across frames must be jointly addressed while preserving instruction-relevant dynamics.

Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to video by defining a spatio-temporal conditional similarity kernel that captures (1) spatial redundancy within frames, (2) temporal redundancy across frames, and (3) instruction-conditioned motion relevance using optical flow features weighted by textual cross-attention. We formulate a hierarchical DPP that first selects a diverse subset of keyframes, then applies conditional diversity pruning within selected frames, jointly optimizing the combined selection. A lightweight temporal coherence regularizer prevents selecting tokens that are individually diverse but temporally incoherent.

Experiments: Evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-Video, and InternVideo2. Compare against image-level CDPruner applied naively to video, FastV, and VideoLLM-online. Measure FLOPs reduction, latency, and accuracy across short/medium/long videos, with ablations on temporal vs. spatial DPP components and varying frame budgets.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video Understanding in MLLMs
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens for image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces an additional temporal dimension where redundancy spans both spatial regions and consecutive frames. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies, leading to either temporal aliasing (dropping key motion events) or excessive retention of static background tokens repeated across frames. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to jointly model spatio-temporal token pruning. We define a conditional similarity kernel over tokens across all frames, incorporating (1) spatial appearance features, (2) temporal optical-flow-derived motion embeddings, and (3) instruction conditioning via cross-attention. A structured DPP over this joint kernel selects a globally diverse subset of (frame, spatial-location) token pairs that maximizes spatio-temporal coverage conditioned on the user query. To keep DPP tractable at video scale, we use a hierarchical two-stage approach: first prune temporally redundant keyframes via DPP, then spatially prune tokens within selected frames. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and NExT-QA benchmarks using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-OneVision. We measure accuracy-FLOPs trade-offs against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and SparseVideo baselines. Ablations isolate motion embedding contributions and temporal versus spatial pruning ratios.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description:

Existing video MLLMs either uniformly sample frames or apply per-frame token pruning independently, ignoring cross-frame token correlations that cause massive redundancy when consecutive frames are visually similar. This leads to extreme computational waste and degraded instruction-following for temporally grounded queries.

Proposed Method: We extend CDPruner's DPP-based conditional diversity framework to jointly model spatial and temporal token selection. We define a 3D conditional similarity kernel that captures (1) spatial similarity within frames, (2) temporal similarity across frames, and (3) instruction-conditioned relevance using both visual and temporal attention signals. We formulate a single DPP over the full spatiotemporal token grid, selecting a globally diverse, instruction-relevant subset that eliminates both intra-frame and inter-frame redundancy simultaneously. To handle the computational scaling of DPP to thousands of tokens, we introduce a hierarchical approximation: frame-level clustering followed by intra-cluster DPP sampling.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, NExT-QA, and ActivityNet-QA using Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-OneVision, and InternVL2. We measure accuracy vs. FLOPs tradeoffs, temporal grounding performance, and wall-clock latency reductions across varying video lengths and temporal query types, comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and uniform sampling baselines.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames and temporally across frames. title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a new dimension of redundancy—temporal redundancy across frames—that existing token pruning methods fail to exploit jointly with spatial redundancy. Naively applying image-level pruning per frame ignores inter-frame correlations, retaining semantically duplicate tokens across time steps and leaving significant computational savings on the table.

Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the spatio-temporal domain. We define a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial token similarity within frames and temporal similarity across frames, conditioned on the user instruction. The combined kernel factorizes into spatial and temporal components with a learned mixing weight. We then apply k-DPP sampling over the full spatio-temporal token set to select a diverse, instruction-relevant subset. Additionally, we propose an efficient chunked DPP approximation to handle the O(N^2) complexity over long video sequences.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using VideoLLaVA, LLaVA-OneVision, and InternVL2 backbones. Ablations compare: (1) per-frame CDPruner, (2) temporal-only pruning, (3) joint spatio-temporal pruning. We report FLOPs reduction, latency, and benchmark accuracy across reduction ratios (50%-90%), demonstrating that temporal modeling yields superior accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs over spatial-only baselines.

title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Hierarchical DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens for image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces an additional temporal dimension where redundancy spans both spatial and temporal axes. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores inter-frame dependencies, while uniform temporal sampling discards motion-critical frames, leading to poor performance on temporally-sensitive tasks like action recognition, temporal grounding, and video QA.

Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to a two-level hierarchical Determinantal Point Process (H-DPP). The first level performs temporal frame selection by computing conditional similarity across frame-level representations conditioned on the textual query, selecting a maximally diverse yet instruction-relevant subset of keyframes. The second level applies spatial token pruning within each selected frame using CDPruner-style conditional DPP. We define cross-frame conditional kernels that penalize temporal redundancy while rewarding motion saliency, computed via optical flow magnitude weighted by instruction attention scores.

Experiments: We evaluate on EgoSchema, NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, and MVBench using LLaVA-Video and Video-LLaMA3 as base models. Ablations compare flat vs. hierarchical DPP, uniform vs. adaptive frame selection, and various reduction ratios (50%-90%). We measure accuracy retention, FLOPs reduction, and latency improvements against baselines including FastV, temporal uniformsampling, and per-frame CDPruner.

title: Temporal-Aware Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding presents a fundamentally harder challenge: tokens must be pruned across both spatial and temporal dimensions simultaneously, where naive frame-level application of DPP ignores inter-frame redundancy and temporal dynamics critical for action/event understanding. Existing video MLLM compression methods either uniformly sample frames or apply image-level pruning per-frame, discarding temporal coherence signals.

Method: We extend CDPruner to video via a Spatio-Temporal DPP (ST-DPP) formulation. We define a joint spatio-temporal kernel that encodes (1) conditional visual-linguistic similarity conditioned on the instruction, (2) temporal position embeddings capturing motion saliency via optical flow differentials between adjacent frames, and (3) cross-frame diversity to penalize selecting near-duplicate tokens across time. The combined kernel enables a single DPP sampling pass over the full video token set, selecting a subset that is both instruction-relevant and maximally diverse across space and time. We further propose an efficient sequential DPP approximation to handle long videos (100+ frames) tractably.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and VideoLLaMA2. Ablations compare spatial-only DPP, temporal-only sampling, and ST-DPP at various token reduction ratios (50%-95%), measuring accuracy, FLOPs, and latency tradeoffs.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively reduces visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy challenge: both spatial redundancy within frames and temporal redundancy across frames. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies, leading to either over-sampling static regions or under-sampling motion-critical tokens relevant to temporal queries like 'what action occurs between timestamps X and Y?'. title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Hierarchical DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens for image-based MLLMs, video understanding presents a dual redundancy challenge: spatial redundancy within frames AND temporal redundancy across frames. Naively applying CDPruner frame-by-frame ignores inter-frame dependencies, while flat application across all video tokens is computationally prohibitive for long videos. Second, a fine spatial-DPP stage applies conditional diversity pruning within each selected keyframe, incorporating both appearance and motion features (frame difference vectors) into the conditional similarity kernel. The two-stage hierarchy is unified under a single conditional diversity objective with learnable stage-wise budget allocation. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video, VideoLLaMA2, and InternVideo2 backbones. We measure accuracy-vs-token-reduction tradeoffs, CUDA latency for videos of varying lengths (30s–10min), and ablate temporal-vs-spatial budget splits. Baseline comparisons include FastV, VidToMe, and frame-uniform sampling.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Spatial and Temporal Dimensions
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes visual tokens in image-based MLLMs via conditional diversity, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy challenge: tokens are redundant not only spatially within frames but also temporally across frames, yet naive extension of spatial DPP pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies and temporal instruction relevance (e.g., 'what happens after the person sits down?' demands temporally-aware selection).

Proposed Method: We introduce TCD-Pruner, which extends DPP-based conditional diversity to a joint spatio-temporal token space. We define a factored conditional similarity kernel that combines (1) spatial token similarity conditioned on instruction semantics within frames, and (2) temporal similarity across frames conditioned on action/event relevance extracted via temporal attention patterns. We then solve a structured DPP over this joint kernel using a block-diagonal approximation for tractability, enabling diverse token selection that spans both spatial regions and temporally informative frames simultaneously. A temporal instruction-relevance scorer using lightweight motion-text cross-attention guides the conditioning.

Experiments: Evaluate on video QA benchmarks (ActivityNet-QA, EgoSchema, MVBench, Video-MME) using VideoLLaVA, LLaVA-Video, and InternVL2-Video. Ablations compare spatial-only DPP, temporal-only DPP, and joint TCD-Pruner. Report FLOPs reduction, latency, and accuracy retention at various compression ratios (50%-95%).

title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP

An adaptive budget allocation mechanism distributes pruning ratios non-uniformly across frames based on per-frame instruction relevance scores.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Spatiotemporal Dimensions
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem where tokens are spatially redundant within frames AND temporally redundant across frames. Naively applying image-level DPP pruning independently per frame ignores inter-frame dependencies, while applying it globally across all video tokens is computationally prohibitive due to O(n³) DPP complexity. Proposed Method: We propose TCD-Pruner, a hierarchical conditional diversity pruning framework for video MLLMs. First, we construct a spatiotemporal conditional similarity matrix that encodes both spatial token relationships within frames and temporal token relationships across frames, conditioned on the textual query. We then apply a two-stage DPP: (1) a frame-level DPP selects maximally diverse keyframes conditioned on the instruction, and (2) a within-frame spatial DPP prunes tokens within selected frames. To handle temporal queries (e.g., 'what happens before X'), we introduce query-aware temporal weighting that modulates the conditional similarity based on predicted temporal relevance. Experiments: We evaluate on video QA benchmarks (EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, MSVD-QA, NExT-QA) using LLaVA-Video and Video-LLaMA architectures, measuring accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs at various reduction ratios, and compare against frame-sampling baselines, per-frame CDPruner, and recent video token compression methods.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face an additional temporal redundancy dimension where thousands of tokens across dozens of frames create prohibitive computational costs. Naive frame-independent pruning ignores cross-frame redundancy, while uniform temporal sampling discards instruction-relevant moments. Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to video by defining a spatiotemporal DPP kernel that captures both within-frame and cross-frame conditional similarity conditioned on the user instruction. The kernel factorizes into a spatial component (adapted from CDPruner) and a temporal coherence component measuring motion-aware feature differences between corresponding tokens across frames. We formulate a hierarchical DPP: first selecting a diverse set of keyframes conditioned on the instruction, then applying conditional spatial pruning within each selected frame. To handle the computational burden of large DPP matrices across hundreds of frames, we introduce a greedy block-diagonal approximation that maintains efficiency while respecting temporal structure. Planned Experiments: Evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA across LLaVA-Video, Video-LLaMA3, and InternVideo2. Measure FLOPs reduction, latency, and accuracy retention at various pruning ratios (50-95%). Ablate spatial-only vs. temporal-only vs. joint pruning and compare against frame sampling baselines and per-frame CDPruner application.

title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Hierarchical DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical temporal dimension where redundancy exists both within frames (spatial) and across frames (temporal). Naively applying CDPruner independently per frame ignores inter-frame dependencies and temporal relevance to instructions like 'what happens after the person picks up the object?', leading to redundant frame-level token retention. Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to video by proposing a hierarchical two-stage DPP formulation. First, a temporal-level DPP selects a diverse yet instruction-relevant subset of keyframes by defining conditional similarity across frame-level representations conditioned on the query. Second, within selected frames, a spatial-level DPP (analogous to CDPruner) prunes intra-frame tokens. We introduce a temporal-aware kernel that encodes both visual similarity and temporal distance, ensuring selected tokens span meaningful temporal spans. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) video QA benchmarks: EgoSchema, NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, MVBench; (2) long-video understanding: Video-MME; (3) efficiency metrics: FLOPs, latency, memory across LLaVA-Video, Video-LLaMA3, and InternVL2-Video with varying compression ratios (50%-95%), comparing against FastV, VideoLLM-online, and frame-sampling baselines.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face an exponentially larger token burden due to temporal redundancy across frames. Naive per-frame pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies, while global pruning ignores frame-level structure. No existing method jointly maximizes spatio-temporal diversity conditioned on user instructions for video MLLMs.

Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the temporal domain by defining a hierarchical two-level DPP. First, a frame-level DPP selects a diverse subset of keyframes conditioned on the instruction, using temporal-aware kernels that encode motion saliency and instruction relevance. Second, a within-frame spatial DPP (analogous to CDPruner) selects spatially diverse tokens from each selected frame. The conditional similarity kernel is augmented with optical flow features to penalize temporally redundant tokens across frames, ensuring the retained token budget captures both spatial detail and temporal dynamics relevant to the query.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and MVBench using VideoLLaVA, Video-LLaMA2, and LLaVA-NeXT-Video. Ablations compare single-level vs. hierarchical DPP, instruction-conditioned vs. unconditional kernels, and various temporal reduction ratios (50%-90%). We measure accuracy, FLOPs reduction, and latency against frame-sampling baselines and FastV.

title: Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical additional dimension: temporal redundancy across frames. Naively extending CDPruner frame-by-frame ignores inter-frame dependencies, while flat pooling across all frames loses temporal structure essential for video QA tasks (e.g., action recognition, temporal grounding). Proposed Method: We introduce VideoCDPruner, which extends the conditional diversity framework to joint spatio-temporal token pruning. We define a factored conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial appearance similarity within frames and temporal motion similarity across frames, conditioned on the text instruction. Using a structured DPP over a 2D spatio-temporal token grid, we maximize conditional diversity jointly across space and time, allowing the model to naturally select keyframes and salient spatial regions simultaneously. The kernel uses optical flow features to encode temporal dissimilarity and instruction-conditioned cross-attention weights to encode query relevance. Planned Experiments: (1) Evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA benchmarks using VideoLLaVA and LLaVA-NeXT-Video. (2) Ablate spatial-only vs. temporal-only vs. joint DPP pruning. (3) Compare against VideoLLaVA's frame sampling, FastV, and frame-level CDPruner at matched FLOPs. (4) Analyze token selection patterns for temporal grounding queries to verify instruction-conditioned temporal focus.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatiotemporal DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames AND temporally across frames. Existing video token reduction methods treat temporal and spatial dimensions independently, missing cross-frame conditional dependencies relative to the user query (e.g., 'What happens after the person falls?').

Proposed Method: We extend CDPruner's conditional diversity framework to joint spatiotemporal token pruning. We define a spatiotemporal conditional similarity kernel that captures (1) spatial similarity within frames, (2) temporal similarity across frames, and (3) instruction-conditioned relevance using cross-attention scores. We reformulate token selection as a structured DPP over a spatiotemporal token graph, enabling the selected subset to maximize both intra-frame diversity and inter-frame temporal coverage conditioned on the instruction. We introduce a hierarchical DPP decomposition to make inference tractable over long video sequences without quadratic cost.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and InternVL-Video backbones. Ablations compare (1) spatial-only DPP, (2) temporal-only DPP, and (3) joint spatiotemporal DPP at token retention ratios of 10-50%. We measure accuracy, FLOPs reduction, and latency on 30-second to 5-minute videos.

title: Adaptive Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Hierarchical DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs using conditional DPP, video MLLMs face an additional temporal redundancy dimension where frames exhibit high inter-frame similarity over time. Naively applying CDPruner frame-by-frame ignores cross-frame dependencies, while flat application across all frames scales poorly with video length. Proposed Method: We propose TemporalCDPruner, a hierarchical DPP-based token pruning framework for video MLLMs. At the coarse level, we define a temporal-conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial content similarity and temporal proximity between tokens across frames, conditioned on the user query. We then apply a two-stage DPP: first selecting a diverse set of keyframes that maximizes temporal-conditional diversity, then performing spatial token pruning within each keyframe using per-frame conditional DPP. The conditional similarity incorporates both CLIP-based visual-textual alignment and temporal positional encodings to weight instruction-relevant moments higher. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and NExT-QA benchmarks using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-Video backbones. We measure accuracy retention vs. FLOPs reduction across pruning ratios (50-95%), compare against frame sampling baselines, FastV, and flat CDPruner, and analyze performance on long-form (>1 min) versus short videos to demonstrate temporal diversity benefits.

title: AdaptiveDPP: Dynamic Token Budget Allocation Across Layers Using Conditional Diversity Signals
description:
Problem: CDPruner applies token pruning at a fixed layer with a uniform retention ratio, ignoring that different transformer layers in MLLMs exhibit vastly different redundancy patterns and that optimal pruning depth/ratio may vary by input complexity and instruction type. Uniform budgets either over-prune informationally dense early layers or under-prune redundant deeper layers, leaving performance gains on the table.

Proposed Method: We extend CDPruner's DPP-based conditional diversity framework into a multi-layer adaptive scheme. First, we derive a layer-wise redundancy score by tracking how much the conditional similarity matrix (visual tokens conditioned on instruction) changes between consecutive layers—high similarity change indicates low redundancy, warranting larger token budgets. Second, we train a lightweight predictor (small MLP) on these redundancy signals to dynamically allocate per-layer token budgets given a global FLOPs constraint. The DPP subset selection is then applied independently at each targeted layer with its allocated budget, propagating only selected tokens forward.

Experiments: (1) Compare against CDPruner and fixed-layer baselines on LLaVA-1.5, InternVL, and Qwen-VL across VQAv2, MMBench, and MMMU. (2) Ablate budget allocation strategies (uniform vs. predicted vs. oracle). (3) Analyze layer-wise redundancy patterns across instruction categories (spatial, counting, OCR). (4) Measure wall-clock latency and FLOPs at matched accuracy targets to quantify efficiency gains over CDPruner.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description: Problem: Video MLLMs face an even more severe token explosion than image MLLMs—a 60-second video at 1fps with 256 tokens/frame yields 15,360 visual tokens, making inference prohibitively expensive. Existing pruning methods treat video frames independently, missing the opportunity to exploit inter-frame redundancy jointly with instruction conditioning. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the video domain by defining a spatio-temporal conditional similarity kernel. For each token, we compute: (1) spatial similarity within a frame, (2) temporal similarity across frames at the same spatial position, and (3) instruction-conditioned relevance via cross-attention scores with the query tokens. We formulate a joint DPP over the full token set (frames × spatial tokens), where the kernel encodes all three factors, and solve it efficiently using a greedy MAP approximation with a sliding temporal window to maintain linear complexity. A lightweight token merging step combines pruned tokens from adjacent frames to preserve motion continuity signals. Planned Experiments: Evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and Video-LLaMA3 as backbones. Ablations isolate contributions of temporal vs. spatial vs. instruction-conditioned diversity. Compare against FastV, SparseVideo, and frame-sampling baselines at matched FLOPs budgets, targeting 85%+ accuracy retention at 90% token reduction.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Guided Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Modeling
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a new dimension of redundancy—temporal redundancy across frames—that existing methods fail to exploit jointly with spatial pruning. Naively applying image-level pruning per frame ignores inter-frame token correlations, retaining temporally repetitive content while discarding unique motion-relevant tokens. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the spatio-temporal domain by defining a joint kernel that captures both intra-frame spatial diversity and inter-frame temporal novelty, conditioned on the textual instruction. Specifically, we construct a unified token set across all frames and define a block-structured kernel matrix where diagonal blocks capture spatial conditional similarity (as in CDPruner) and off-diagonal blocks encode temporal redundancy between corresponding tokens across adjacent frames. The DPP then selects a globally diverse subset that spans distinct spatial regions and temporally novel frames while remaining instruction-relevant. To keep the DPP tractable for long videos, we propose a hierarchical two-stage selection: coarse frame selection via temporal DPP, followed by fine-grained spatial pruning per selected frame. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and MVBench using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-Video backbones, measuring accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs, latency reduction, and temporal reasoning preservation across varying video lengths (30s–10min).

title: Temporal-Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames AND temporally across frames. Naively applying image-level pruning independently per frame ignores inter-frame dependencies and temporal instruction relevance (e.g., 'what happens after the person sits down?' demands preserving temporally-dispersed, causally-relevant tokens). Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to a joint spatio-temporal setting. We define a temporal-conditional similarity kernel that captures (1) spatial similarity within frames conditioned on the instruction, (2) temporal similarity across frames capturing motion and redundancy, and (3) instruction-temporal relevance weighting that upweights tokens from time intervals most pertinent to the query. We formulate a structured DPP over the full spatio-temporal token grid, using a Kronecker-factored kernel (spatial ⊗ temporal) to make exact MAP inference tractable. A lightweight temporal saliency signal derived from frame-level attention to instruction tokens guides the temporal component. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA using Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-OneVision, and InternVideo2. We compare against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and VideoAgent under matched FLOPs budgets, reporting accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs across short and long video benchmarks.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection to Spatiotemporal Redundancy
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively reduces spatial visual token redundancy in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded challenge: massive spatiotemporal token sequences (frames × spatial tokens) with both intra-frame spatial redundancy and inter-frame temporal redundancy, making naive application of image-pruning methods insufficient. Proposed Method: We propose VideoCDPruner, a hierarchical two-stage DPP-based pruning framework. First, a temporal DPP stage selects a diverse yet instruction-relevant subset of keyframes by defining conditional similarity across frames conditioned on the textual query. Second, a spatial DPP stage applies conditional diversity maximization within each selected frame, jointly conditioning on both the instruction and the temporal context of neighboring frames. The inter-frame conditioning captures temporal dependencies, preventing selection of visually similar patches across consecutive retained frames. Both stages remain training-free and use efficient greedy DPP approximations for scalability. Experiments: We evaluate on video QA benchmarks (EgoSchema, MVBench, Video-MME, ActivityNet-QA) using Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-Next-Video, and InternVL2-Video. We measure accuracy retention at 80-95% token reduction ratios, CUDA latency, and FLOPs. Ablations isolate temporal vs. spatial DPP stages, and compare against frame-sampling baselines, uniform spatial pruning, and video-specific attention methods like FastV.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs: Extending DPP-Based Token Selection Across Frames
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively reduces visual token redundancy in image-based MLLMs using conditional DPP, video MLLMs face a fundamentally harder challenge: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames and temporally across frames, while instruction relevance varies dynamically over the video timeline. Naively applying per-frame CDPruner ignores cross-frame temporal dependencies and may discard tokens capturing motion or state transitions critical to answering temporal questions.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalCDPruner, which extends the DPP formulation to jointly model spatial and temporal token diversity. We construct a unified kernel that encodes (1) conditional similarity between spatial tokens within frames given the instruction, (2) temporal coherence across corresponding tokens in adjacent frames, and (3) instruction-conditioned temporal saliency scores that weight frames based on semantic relevance to time-sensitive queries. The DPP objective jointly selects a subset of (frame, spatial-token) pairs maximizing spatio-temporal conditional diversity, with an efficient approximation using structured block-diagonal kernel decomposition to keep inference tractable.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and NeXT-QA benchmarks using LLaVA-Video and Video-LLaMA3 backbones. We compare against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and SparseVideoLLM at varying token budgets (50%-90% reduction), measuring accuracy, FLOPs, and latency to demonstrate superior temporal reasoning preservation.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Aware Token Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical additional dimension: temporal redundancy across frames. Naively applying per-frame CDPruner ignores inter-frame correlations, either over-pruning unique temporal events or retaining redundant near-duplicate frames. Existing video MLLM token reduction methods (e.g., FastV, token merging) fail to jointly optimize spatial diversity within frames and temporal diversity across frames conditioned on the query instruction. We define a block-structured kernel matrix that captures (1) intra-frame conditional similarity as in CDPruner and (2) inter-frame temporal similarity weighted by motion magnitude (optical flow or frame differencing). A hierarchical DPP sampling strategy first selects a diverse subset of keyframes conditioned on the instruction, then applies conditional spatial DPP within each selected frame. The inter-frame kernel incorporates temporal positional encoding to preserve narrative coherence. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames and temporally across frames. Naively applying spatial DPP to each frame independently ignores inter-frame correlations, while flat application across all frames scales poorly (O(n³) DPP complexity for n total tokens). First, we define a joint spatio-temporal conditional similarity that combines spatial patch similarity with temporal optical-flow-aware similarity, conditioned on the textual query. Second, we decompose the DPP into two stages: (1) a temporal DPP selecting a diverse subset of key frames conditioned on the instruction, and (2) per-selected-frame spatial DPP pruning tokens within those frames. This decomposition reduces complexity from O((T×S)³) to O(T³ + K×S³) where T=frames, S=spatial tokens, K=selected frames. We further introduce a motion-aware kernel that upweights temporally dynamic regions. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and Video-LLaMA. Ablations compare flat-DPP, frame-uniform sampling, and hierarchical variants, measuring accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs across reduction ratios 50%-95%.

title: Temporal CDPruning: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination

We reformulate token pruning as a DPP over the full spatio-temporal token grid, with a structured kernel that decomposes into spatial and temporal components for tractable inference via low-rank approximations. A temporal saliency weighting term prioritizes tokens from frames most relevant to the query. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video backbones, measuring accuracy vs. FLOPs tradeoff at multiple reduction ratios (50%-95%), comparing against uniform sampling, FastV, and frame-level CDPruner baselines.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a dual redundancy challenge: spatial redundancy within frames AND temporal redundancy across frames. We define a conditional kernel matrix over the full token set spanning all frames, where similarity is conditioned on both the textual instruction and temporal position embeddings. We introduce a structured DPP with a factored kernel: K = K_spatial ⊗ K_temporal + K_cross, where K_cross captures instruction-conditioned cross-frame dependencies. To handle the computational challenge of large DPP inference over thousands of video tokens, we propose a hierarchical two-stage sampling: first select keyframes via temporal DPP, then apply spatial DPP within selected frames. Experiments: We evaluate on VideoMME, ActivityNet-QA, EgoSchema, and NExT-QA benchmarks using LLaVA-Video, Video-LLaVA, and MiniCPT-V as base models. title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video-Language Models via Causal DPP

The method remains training-free and pluggable into existing video-LLMs. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA across multiple video-LLMs (Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-Video, InternVideo2). Ablations isolate contributions of temporal causality constraints, the cross-frame kernel, and reduction ratios (50%-95%). title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video-Language Models via Spatio-Temporal DPP

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Efficient Video Understanding in MLLMs
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens for image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical temporal dimension where redundancy exists both within frames (spatial) and across frames (temporal). Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores cross-frame dependencies, leading to either over-pruning temporally unique events or retaining near-duplicate frames that differ only slightly across time.

Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to a hierarchical spatio-temporal setting called TemporalCDPruner. First, we define a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial similarity within frames and temporal similarity across frames, conditioned on the textual instruction. We decompose the DPP into a two-stage process: (1) temporal frame selection via a DPP over frame-level representations to maximize instruction-conditioned temporal diversity, and (2) spatial token pruning within selected frames using CDPruner. Additionally, we introduce a motion-aware conditioning term that up-weights tokens corresponding to high temporal change regions, ensuring dynamic events aligned with the query are preserved.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and VideoLLaMA2. Baselines include FastV, SparseVideoLLM, and per-frame CDPruner. We measure accuracy-FLOPs tradeoffs at varying reduction ratios (50-95%) and analyze temporal event localization quality.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatiotemporal DPP
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy challenge: massive temporal duplication across frames compounds spatial redundancy within frames, making naïve per-frame token pruning insufficient. Existing video MLLM compression methods treat temporal and spatial dimensions independently, missing cross-frame conditional dependencies.

Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to a joint spatiotemporal setting. We define a spatiotemporal conditional similarity kernel that captures both intra-frame spatial redundancy and inter-frame temporal redundancy, conditioned on the textual query. We formulate a hierarchical DPP over the combined token space: a frame-level DPP first selects a diverse set of keyframes conditioned on the instruction, followed by a spatial DPP within each selected frame that accounts for already-selected tokens from other frames. This two-stage decomposition makes the otherwise intractable joint DPP over thousands of video tokens computationally feasible while remaining training-free and model-agnostic.

Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, ActivityNet-QA, and EgoSchema using LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video. We compare against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and temporal pooling baselines at various token budgets. Ablations study the hierarchical decomposition vs. joint optimization and temporal kernel design choices. Target: 90%+ accuracy retention with 85%+ FLOPs reduction.

title: AdaptiveDPP: Online Conditional Diversity Pruning for Streaming Video Understanding in MLLMs
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes visual tokens for static images, video MLLMs face a compounding challenge: temporal redundancy across frames creates massive token sequences (e.g., 64 frames × 256 tokens = 16,384 tokens) that overwhelm even aggressive spatial pruning. Naively applying CDPruner frame-by-frame ignores inter-frame redundancy, while pooling across frames loses temporal instruction-relevant details. Proposed Method: We introduce AdaptiveDPP, an online token pruning framework for video MLLMs that extends DPP-based conditional diversity to the temporal dimension. First, we define cross-frame conditional similarity that accounts for both spatial content overlap and temporal proximity, conditioned on the instruction. Second, we reformulate the DPP kernel to operate over a sliding temporal window, enabling tokens selected in earlier frames to inform selection in later frames through a 'diversity memory' mechanism. Third, we introduce instruction-adaptive kernel reweighting that dynamically adjusts spatial vs. temporal diversity trade-offs based on query type (e.g., causal reasoning favors temporal spread; object queries favor spatial diversity). The method remains training-free. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video backbones, measuring accuracy-vs-FLOPs trade-offs at 70-95% token reduction ratios, comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and temporal pooling baselines.

title: Temporal CDPruning: Conditional Diversity-Guided Visual Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Modeling

Experiments: Evaluate on video QA benchmarks (EgoSchema, NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, MVBench), temporal reasoning tasks, and long-video understanding (Video-MME). Compare against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and video-specific pruning baselines across LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video at varying compression ratios (50%-95% token reduction), measuring accuracy, FLOPs, and latency.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video-Language Models via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video-language models face a compounded redundancy challenge: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames and temporally across frames. Naively applying image-based pruning independently per frame ignores inter-frame dependencies, leading to redundant retention of near-identical tokens across consecutive frames. Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to the spatio-temporal domain by formulating a joint Spatio-Temporal DPP (ST-DPP) over the full video token set. We define conditional similarity that accounts for both spatial proximity within frames and temporal proximity across frames, conditioned on the text query. The DPP kernel is factored into spatial and temporal components with learnable weighting, enabling efficient approximation via a two-stage greedy DPP: first selecting diverse keyframes conditioned on the query, then selecting spatially diverse tokens within selected frames. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using VideoLLaVA, LLaVA-Video, and InternVideo2. We measure accuracy-latency tradeoffs at various reduction ratios (50%-95% token budgets), comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and temporal pooling baselines. We additionally analyze keyframe selection quality against ground-truth temporal annotations.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description: Problem: Video understanding in MLLMs faces an acute token explosion—a 1-minute video at 1fps yields 60× more visual tokens than a single image. Existing video token reduction methods either uniformly sample frames or apply per-frame spatial pruning independently, failing to exploit cross-frame temporal redundancy while maintaining instruction-relevant content across the temporal dimension. Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework from CDPruner to the spatio-temporal domain by proposing Temporal CDPruner (T-CDPruner). We define a joint conditional similarity metric that captures both spatial (within-frame patch similarity) and temporal (across-frame feature similarity) redundancy, conditioned on the textual instruction. We reformulate video token pruning as a single DPP optimization over the full 3D token grid, where the quality term weights tokens by instruction-conditioned attention scores and the diversity kernel penalizes both spatially and temporally similar tokens. To make DPP tractable over thousands of tokens, we introduce a hierarchical greedy DPP solver that first performs inter-frame selection then intra-frame refinement. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and InternVL2-Video backbones, comparing against FastV, Frame Sampling, and MovieChat. We analyze token retention distributions across temporal and spatial dimensions and measure latency on 4-minute videos at varying reduction ratios (70-95%).

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatiotemporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face an exponentially larger token burden—a 30-second video at 1fps with 256 tokens/frame yields 7,680 tokens before any text. Naive application of CDPruner independently per frame ignores temporal redundancy (near-duplicate frames) and cross-frame conditional diversity, leading to suboptimal compression for video. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the spatiotemporal domain. We define a joint spatiotemporal kernel that captures (1) within-frame spatial diversity conditioned on the instruction (inheriting CDPruner's conditional similarity), (2) cross-frame temporal diversity penalizing selection of visually redundant tokens across adjacent frames, and (3) temporal saliency weights derived from optical flow magnitude to prioritize dynamic regions. The resulting Temporal-CDPruner solves a structured DPP over a spatiotemporal token graph, enabling joint selection of tokens across frames that maximize instruction-relevant, temporally diverse coverage. We apply a hierarchical approximation (per-segment DPP followed by cross-segment DPP) to keep inference tractable. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, MVBench, and ActivityNet-QA using LLaVA-Video and VideoChat2, measuring accuracy-FLOPs tradeoff at 70-95% token reduction ratios, comparing against FastV, SparseVideo, and per-frame CDPruner baselines.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs with Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces an additional temporal dimension where massive redundancy exists both within frames and across consecutive frames. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores inter-frame correlations, leading to either over-retention of temporally redundant tokens or loss of motion-critical information. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the spatiotemporal domain by defining a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial appearance similarity and temporal motion coherence across frames, conditioned on the textual query. We reformulate the token pruning problem as a single unified DPP over the full spatiotemporal token grid, where the kernel encodes (1) CLIP-based semantic similarity between tokens conditioned on instruction embeddings, (2) optical-flow-derived motion saliency to preserve tokens encoding meaningful temporal change, and (3) a temporal diversity penalty discouraging selection of near-duplicate tokens across adjacent frames. A greedy k-DPP approximation enables tractable inference. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, and NExT-QA benchmarks using LLaVA-Video and VideoChat2 backbones. We measure accuracy-vs-token-reduction trade-offs, FLOPs reduction, and latency improvements, comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and video-specific methods like SlowFast-LLaVA token compression.

title: Temporal CDPruner: Conditional Diversity-Based Token Pruning for Video MLLMs via Cross-Frame Redundancy Elimination
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces a critical additional redundancy dimension: temporal redundancy across frames. Naively applying per-frame spatial pruning ignores cross-frame token correlations, retaining semantically duplicate tokens across time steps and failing to leverage the temporal structure of video queries (e.g., 'what happens after X?'). This leads to suboptimal compression for video MLLMs like Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-NeXT-Video. Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to the spatio-temporal domain. We define a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial appearance similarity and temporal proximity between tokens across frames, conditioned on the textual instruction. A structured DPP over this joint kernel simultaneously selects a diverse subset of tokens across all frames, penalizing spatially similar tokens within a frame and temporally redundant tokens across frames while rewarding instruction relevance. We introduce a lightweight temporal decay factor that upweights tokens from frames most relevant to temporally-grounded queries. The method remains training-free and model-agnostic. Experiments: We evaluate on video QA benchmarks (EgoSchema, NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, MVBench), comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and SparseVideoLLM. We measure accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs at various token budgets and analyze temporal grounding quality.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Video MLLMs via Spatio-Temporal DPP
description: Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding models face a compounded redundancy problem: tokens are redundant both spatially within frames AND temporally across frames. Naive application of spatial pruning independently per frame ignores inter-frame correlations, retaining near-duplicate tokens across consecutive frames and missing temporally sparse but semantically critical events. Proposed Method: We extend the conditional diversity framework to a spatio-temporal DPP formulation. We define a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial appearance similarity within frames and temporal motion/semantic similarity across frames, conditioned on the instruction. The kernel factorizes as a product of a spatial diversity term (per CDPruner) and a temporal novelty term (computed via optical flow-guided feature differences and cross-frame attention). We solve the DPP subset selection jointly across all frames simultaneously, enabling tokens from pivotal temporal moments to be selected even if spatially redundant within their frame. A lightweight two-stage approximation (frame-level DPP selection followed by spatial DPP within selected frames) ensures tractable inference. Experiments: We evaluate on Video-MME, MVBench, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet-QA using Video-LLaVA and LLaVA-Video backbones, measuring accuracy vs. FLOPs reduction at various pruning ratios, comparing against per-frame CDPruner, FastV, and SlowFast token pruning baselines.

title: Temporal Conditional Diversity Pruning for Efficient Video Understanding in MLLMs
description:
Problem: While CDPruner effectively prunes spatial visual tokens in image-based MLLMs, video understanding introduces an additional temporal dimension where redundancy exists both spatially within frames and temporally across frames. Naively applying per-frame token pruning ignores inter-frame dependencies, causing important motion dynamics to be discarded while retaining temporally redundant static content.

Proposed Method: We extend the DPP-based conditional diversity framework to a spatio-temporal setting by defining a joint conditional similarity kernel that captures both spatial redundancy within frames and temporal redundancy across frames, conditioned on the textual instruction. We formulate a two-stage DPP: first, a temporal DPP selects a diverse, instruction-relevant keyframe subset by modeling frame-level embeddings; second, a spatial DPP within each selected keyframe prunes redundant tokens. The temporal kernel incorporates optical flow signals and inter-frame feature differences to explicitly encode motion relevance, ensuring action-critical frames are prioritized under motion-sensitive instructions.

Experiments: We evaluate on video QA benchmarks (EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, MVBench, Video-MME) using video-capable MLLMs (LLaVA-Video, VideoLLaMA2, InternVL-Video). We measure accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs at various token budgets, ablate temporal vs. spatial pruning stages, and compare against frame-sampling baselines and existing video token compression methods. We also analyze instruction-conditioned behavior under action-focused vs. appearance-focused queries.
